articles.title: ‘Cockroach’ party rally: leader detained at airport as Delhi faces large youth protest
articles.cleaned_content:
‘Cockroach’ party rally: leader detained at airport as Delhi faces large youth protest

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke detained at airport, as police patrol capital amid growing demands chief election officer resigns

Police in New Delhi detained scores of protesters on Saturday – including Cockroach Janta party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipkeas – as ⁠thousands of officers and paramilitaries ⁠patrolled India’s capital to guard against a youth protest demanding India’s chief election officer quit.

The protesters, led by the “Cockroach” youth movement, want the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, to quit over a revision of voter lists that critics say favours prime minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata party. Metro stations were shut and mobile internet suspended in Delhi ahead of the arrival of protesters.

Television images showed police in the city’s central business district⁠ chasing down a few dozen young protesters, before they were loaded into vehicles and taken away.

About 200 protesters were detained in the area, a police source told Reuters. Those detained outside Delhi included protest supporter Dhruv Rathee, a popular figure on YouTube, a police spokesperson said.

Before the protest began, police detained Dipke at Delhi airport after he ‌flew in from Mumbai, and reportedly asked ​him to call off the protest as authorities had banned it. Two other CJP ⁠leaders Saurav Das and ​Ashutosh ​Ranka were also ​detained from their flight ​upon ‌landing, the ​movement ​said in a statement.

Touted by organisers as a protest to “save democracy”, it ⁠aims to be the biggest of the demonstrations that were launched last week after the Indian Express newspaper reported that Kumar’s deputies ​had questioned and disagreed with him over the revision process ‌that saw about 130 million ‌voter names removed.

Opposition parties have long alleged the government is trying to fix voter lists to its advantage.

Kumar has not commented. The election commission and the BJP have denied the allegations.

The BJP says Modi’s popularity and India’s economic growth are some of the reasons for its electoral dominance and that opposition parties are misleading the country because they are unable to win elections.

Near daily protests by opposition groups pose a new political challenge to Modi, just months after similar demonstrations forced his education minister to quit over exam paper ‌leaks.

It also comes months before a series of important state elections starting in early 2027, including in the BJP-ruled most populous state of Uttar Pradesh.

The protesters, led by the self-named Cockroach Janta party, that began ​as an online satire, said they would gather at Jantar Mantar on Saturday morning – a site designated for protests by authorities in the heart of New Delhi.

Delhi police said on Friday they had not given permission for the protest because the request did not come on time, adding that CJP had violated undertakings given during previous protests, and that authorities had ⁠to enforce the law and maintain peace.

Police said protesters would face the force of ​the law if they violated the ban.

Tens of thousands of police officers and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across the capital, with multiple layers of yellow metal barricades blocking roads leading to Jantar Mantar.

CJP ​leaders rejected the police decision and said ​they would go ahead with the protest.

Authorities have ordered the closure of dozens of metro stations, and cancelled several trains coming to New Delhi. However, the supreme court on Friday said some trains must still run and there should be no blanket closure of metro stations.

“The dictator would rather shut down the entire national capital and inconvenience millions of citizens than allow a peaceful protest at a designated protest site,” the CJP chief, Dipke, posted on X before he was detained in Delhi.

“Imagine how many lives would be affected because of this shutdown by Modi.”

Mobile internet services in a radius of 4km (2.5 miles) of the protest area were ordered suspended from Friday night to Saturday night, ANI news agency reported citing a government order.

The CJP has said “at least 10,000 people”, including protesters travelling to Delhi by train, have been detained across the country.

Some people detained in the central state of Madhya Pradesh were taken to hotels, The Hindu newspaper reported.

Police have not responded to the party’s broader allegations of mass detentions.

* With Reuters and Agence France-Presse

articles.title: Delhi Police Crackdown: CJP Leaders Detained, Metro Suspended, and Internet Shutdown
articles.cleaned_content:
Delhi became a fortress in the early hours of October 10, with hundreds of protesters detained, 45 metro stations shut down, and a near-total internet blackout in central Delhi, especially within a few kilometres of all roads leading to Jantar Mantar .

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) had called a protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Delhi Police denied permission, saying in a letter to the CJP that the protest could lead to serious law and order problems and that the party’s communication was an intimation, not an application filed at least 10 days in advance, as the guidelines for Jantar Mantar require.

The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation said entry and exit gates at 45 stations would stay closed until further notice, with interchange facilities available at all but the New Delhi station. Internet services were to be suspended within a 4-km radius of Jantar Mantar from 10 pm on October 9 to 10 pm on October 10, according to agency reports.

This came a day after the Supreme Court, on October 9, expressed concern over the closure of metro stations and cancellation of trains, and cautioned the government against using a “hammer to kill a fly” in its security preparations to counter the proposed CJP protest. The bench, led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, said there could be no complete prohibition on the movement of metro trains. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre and Delhi Police, told the court that “some leeway has to be given to the security forces”.

While CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, and Saurav Das were detained inside the aircraft as soon as they landed at Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport, the YouTuber and social influencer Dhruv Rathee was taken into preventive custody beforehand. CJP legal team head Ratna Singh was also detained.

Delhi Police pressed a large number of women personnel into service to deal with the women protesters, apparently to ward off a repeat of previous complaints that some male police personnel had manhandled and misbehaved with women protesters. PTI reported on October 8 that the police had issued specific instructions to personnel on handling women protesters. Even in the CJP leaders’ detention at IGI Airport, women cops were in the forefront, and it was they who interacted with Dipke even as the CJP leaders kept asking them to send the male officers to talk to them.

In Connaught Place, the shopping and social hub in the heart of the city, cops had a tough time detaining young protesters, who were not allowed to proceed further and were pushed into buses parked in large numbers to take them away after their preventive detention.

A large posse of police was seen near the Regal Cinema. As visuals of cops moving in open jeeps and shops shut in Connaught Place circulated, a television channel also showed spike strips ready for use on roads near Mohan Estate, which joins Haryana with Delhi.

Cops also stopped motorcycle-borne youths and youngsters travelling in autos to Delhi railway stations, and manned roads and walkways to metro stations such as Akshardham. Many vehicles entering central Delhi from Noida were forced to return.

After being taken into custody, Dipke said that even Indira Gandhi did not take such measures during the Emergency. He said: “This is dictatorship. You can see where the nation is heading. They [Delhi Police] are here to arrest us directly from the flight. We are not afraid of getting arrested.…”

Before boarding the flight, he had posted on X, “Modi has accepted defeat even before our protest has begun. The mass crackdown on protesters and the shutdown of Delhi are not signs of strength, but of a leader terrified of his own people.”

Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, whose party, the Congress, has not declared any open support for the CJP and is carrying out its protest on the SIR issue separately from it, posted on X, “Gyanesh Kumar will go. This government will go. Then the repair of democracy will begin.” Gandhi and other INDIA bloc MPs have been protesting against Kumar since October 6, and Delhi Police detained him on October 6 and 7.

BJP president Nitin Nabin accused the Congress and other opposition parties of “trying to destabilise the nation at the behest of foreign powers” and of not respecting the people’s mandate for the BJP, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Nabin said the government will fight this out firmly.

This is a developing story. Figures and statements will be updated.

articles.title: Thousands of security personnel deployed as Delhi braces for ‘cockroach’ protest
articles.cleaned_content:
Police have been deployed in big numbers even during demonstrations by opposition parties in the lead up to Saturday's 'cockroach' protest

Parts of the Indian capital, Delhi, have been turned into a fortress, with tens of thousands of security forces deployed, as the influential Gen Z-led "cockroach" movement has called for a major protest on Saturday.

The protesters are seeking electoral reforms and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of manipulating voters' lists.

The Election Commission has denied this and Kumar is yet to comment on calls for his resignation.

The protest comes just months after the movement brought thousands of young people onto Delhi's streets in July, in demonstrations that saw violent clashes with police and forced India's education minister to resign.

Police say they have denied permission for Saturday's gathering, and all roads leading to Jantar Mantar, the main protest venue, have been closed off with huge metal barricades.

The restrictions have caused major disruption across central Delhi, with traffic diverted from several key roads. A journey that would normally take 15 minutes took more than an hour this morning.

At Jantar Mantar, police and paramilitary personnel are stationed behind barricades and ropes, preventing people from entering the protest site. Drones could be seen flying overhead.

Some protesters who arrived early were stopped and questioned by security personnel. The BBC also saw at least five people being detained near the site.

Journalists covering the protest have been cordoned off into a designated area nearby.

At a nearby roundabout, loudspeakers repeatedly broadcast appeals for people to cooperate with the police.

Delhi Police has defended the measures, saying they were necessary to maintain public safety and prevent overcrowding at Jantar Mantar, which can accommodate only 1,000 people at a time.

Sabika Muzaffar has travelled from nearby Haryana state with her mother to take part in Saturday's protest

Several trains to Delhi have also been cancelled and police have ordered dozens of metro stations shut to prevent protesters from gathering.

But Abhijeet Dipke, founder ⁠of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) - the online satirical movement that is spearheading the protests - has said the CJP will march to Jantar Mantar on Saturday morning "come what may".

"If you want to jail us or even shoot us we are prepared," he added, addressing ​Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a post on X.

The CJP first emerged as a major protest movement during weeks of demonstrations demanding education reforms over the summer. The resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan in July was seen as a major victory for the group.

CJP protesters returned to the streets last week with a rally in Mumbai to demand Kumar's resignation. On Thursday, they held another large rally in the southern city of Bengaluru (formerly Bangalore).

Student groups and opposition parties have also protested in the capital over the past few days.

The CJP held a rally in Bengaluru city on Thursday against CEC Kumar

Saturday's protests are being billed as the biggest in recent times as they are also being supported by several opposition parties, farmer organisations and student groups.

CJP leaders allege the authorities have been preventing many of their supporters from reaching Delhi.

In the capital, more than 30,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed and authorities have appealed to citizens to stay away from protests.

Police official Nupur Prasad told a press conference , external that one of the reasons for denying permission to protest at Jantar Mantar was the "short notice" given by the CJP.

"Under current guidelines, an application to organise an event at Jantar Mantar must be submitted at least 10 days prior to the scheduled date," she said.

Also, she added that in the past, the CJP had not followed "lawful directions" given to them.

"In light of the non-compliance with prescribed procedures, the failure to adhere to past legal directions, and the current state of public safety, law and order, and traffic regulation, permission for the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar is hereby denied."

The CJP have questioned police denying them permission for the protest - they say that legally they only have to inform the police and do not need their approval to gather.

Gyanesh Kumar is at the centre of the voter-roll revision controversy

At the centre of the row is a controversial revision of the country's electoral rolls known as the Special Intensive Revision, or SIR, which began last year.

The Election Commission says it is to remove duplicate and ineligible entries - and so far, 130 million names have been struck off the voters' list.

But opposition parties and activists have alleged that many of those are eligible voters and that the process is being manipulated by CEC Kumar to favour Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) during elections. Both the BJP and the Election Commission have rejected the accusations.

The past few days have also seen a major escalation in the opposition's standoff with the Election Commission.

For three days in a row starting Tuesday, Delhi witnessed dramatic scenes with police breaking up protests by opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and other MPs over the issue.

Videos showing police forcing Gandhi on to a bus and preventing him from climbing out of the bus window subsequently went viral on social media.
